opportunity: On every big-endian 32-bit ABI a two-register value comes back with the HIGH word in the first register (PowerPC r3, MIPS o32 $2, SPARC %o0, ARM BE r0; AArch64 BE x0 for __int128), and AVR's gcc ABI returns an int with the high byte in R25, the first register of its reversesignif join rule. Return recovery and the call-output pair joined that register as the low half, so clang -O2 `long long wide_mul(int,int)` printed `CONCAT44(a1 * a0,(int)(... >> 0x20))` on PowerPC, MIPS, SPARC and ARM big-endian, and AVR `int negate(int)` printed `CONCAT11(a1,a0)`.

change_kind: correctness-fix behind option bejoin (default on): only the join order of a returned or call-output register pair whose output rule joins the first register high changes, and only when the function's low word looks returned on purpose; little-endian targets never take the new order, and off is byte-identical to main. It is an option because the rule is a prior: an int holding the high word of a 64-bit temporary, its stale low half left in the second register, can compile to the same registers as the long long and reads as it
inspiration: upstream FuncCallSpecs::buildOutputFromTrials reads ParamActive::isJoinReverse; ActionReturnRecovery::buildReturnOutput does not
parity: make test 675/675 PARITY OK; make test-stages 1828/1828 PARITY OK (on fefd8911e: main's 1795 stage keys plus the 33 bejoin keys)
root_cause: buildReturnOutput and kuna_rustabi::build_call_output_pair took trial 0 (the first register) as the low half although the <join/> output rule records that it consumed the most significant piece first (big-endian register spaces, and AVR through reversesignif). Joining in the ABI's order is only right when the second register is the low word: a function returning one register often leaves something there (SPARC's restore hands %i1 back in %o1; clang -O0 MIPS leaves a dead zero in $3; scratch values), and every pass that narrows such a pair back to the first register (the uncomputed-half repair, bool/byte narrowing, C's truncation in a narrow prototype) keeps the right register only with the old join.
fix: kuna_bejoin::join_order classifies the second register at every live RETURN at return recovery: halves of one wider value made by an operation (Wide), a value or nonzero literal read only by the pair's RETURN slots (Returned), a literal zero (Zero), a clobber or never-written location (Nothing), the register's own entry value with no instruction moving it (Entry), a value also used elsewhere, reaching the first register other than through its sign, a comparison or as the other half of a wider value, or the stack pointer (Scratch), what a 64-bit comparison left behind (Compared: the first register holds a computed 0 or 1 by its possibly-nonzero bits -- comparisons, carries, sign bits, a leading-zero count shifted to its top bit, 0s and 1s chosen between -- or a literal 0 or 1 where the function's live RETURNs hold both, a boolean a branch chose, or the low word is a sum or difference -- not a move spelled as adding or subtracting zero; 0 - x counts -- and nothing a comparison, carry or borrow produced, nor the low word itself, reaches a first register that is more than one literal, or the low word is such a sum or difference whose carry or borrow -- a comparison of only its operands and itself, through copies and truncations (carries_of) -- reaches a conditional branch or the first register (tests_carry) while the first register is worked out from comparisons and literals alone: a literal, a value with at most one settable bit, or such values negated, offset, shifted, masked, added or chosen between, a choice's input its edge's branch tested equal to a literal counting as that literal, and the sum's own carry never one of them (of_flags)), or an -O0 int truncation (Truncated: both registers loaded from adjacent words of one stack object off the entry stack pointer, the first from the less significant word, the reverse of a long long's reload, unless each word is its own register's argument home); Compared and Truncated only where one register holds a whole int, so not AVR. A division by a constant (Quotient: the low word is SUBPIECE(p, 0) of an INT_MULT at least two words wide and the product's high half reaches the first register through a right shift by a literal on some path -- ARM BE umull r1,r0,r2,r3; lsr r0,r0,#3 for a / 10 -- divided_down) also keeps main's join, on every target. The backward walk follows the low word's byte range through copies, phis, indirects and register pieces; window save/restore copies do not count as moves. ABI order iff option bejoin is on and some RETURN is Wide or Returned and none is Entry, Scratch, Compared, Truncated, Quotient or ShiftedOut (a right shift whose dropped bits reach the first register: a 64-bit temporary held the reverse way round, ARM BE `lsrs r1,r1,#1; rrx r0,r0`), and a Returned one vetoes too when the function has an indirect jump flow could not follow and one of the values the low word is made from is an input, a literal or made in a block dominating the jump (unfollowed_jumps, reaches_jump); an int worked out from the high half of a 64-bit temporary vetoes too (Reworked: with high and low paired through moves -- PowerPC mr is or 3,5,5, MIPS move is or with $zero -- and same-block choices, a low-word sum or difference whose carry or borrow reaches the first register other than as that sum's own high word, each flag entering with its sign -- carry added, borrow subtracted, MIPS a < a - b, a negation's b != 0 -- read through truncations and loop choices, a shift, mask, product, literal or wrong-signed flag on the way being a rework and a piece of a wider value counting for nothing (carried_into, carry_signs, value_key, Terms::walk); a low word chosen where the first register is not is judged per sum, a sum whose own high word is the first register counting as 64-bit; with no carry between them, a first register that is a literal operation -- shift, mask, offset, negation, product, or/xor with a literal -- on a value the low word never reads, following the first register only into a stack slot stored once, unless the low word gets the same bitwise operation (works_over, worked_operand, sources, reads, parallel)); so does the high half of a product beside a first register that reads its low half (ProductHigh: product_high_half, reads_low_half, following stack reloads; stack_offset now reads MIPS move $fp,$sp), and a Returned low word made where an operation with no register inputs (an inline system call, PowerPC sc as syscall()) can read it (hidden_readers, beside the unfollowed jumps); otherwise main's order, and Funcdata::kuna_pairs_first_low makes that function's call-output pairs main's order too. The uncomputed-half repair skips pairs joined first register high. pair_join_address keeps a join record when the contiguous pair's parent register is global (AVR R25R24). The previous version's register-window machinery (WindowPair, zero_leftover_low_half, narrow_window_pair, late literal/ZEXT look-throughs) and its substrate change are removed.

tradeoff.read_as_long_long_wrong_for_int: an int holding the high word of a 64-bit temporary itself, whose stale low half stays in the second register, in the long long's registers: (int)((a+b)>>32) and (int)((a-b)>>32) on PowerPC/ARM BE/SPARC -O1/-O2 (the code for a+b; gcc -O0 on MIPS moves the word down with srl $17,$2,0 and keeps the int), ((u64)a*b)>>32 on ARM BE at every -O (umull r1,r0 writes both registers) and MIPS gcc -O0 (multu, mflo/mfhi). MIPS gcc -O0 (u32)(*p >> 32) loads both words of *p into $2:$3 as return *p does. The same for (u32)(((u64)a*b + c) >> 32) and (u32)((x*3) >> 32) of a u64, and for an unsigned division by a constant whose magic number needs no shift (a / 641, a / 6700417: a bare umull r1,r0,r0,r1 on ARM BE at every -O, printed as the product). Main printed these right; on prints the whole 64-bit value; off prints them right again. -O0 absolute values, selects and min/max truncated to int reload the temporary low word first and now keep their int. A division by a constant whose magic-number product is shifted down, which leaves the product's low half in the second register on ARM BE, keeps its int, and so does an int that is a 64-bit sum, difference or product shifted right by one in the reverse pair (ARM BE at every -O, and clang -O0 (u32)(x>>1) of a 64-bit argument). (u32)((x + K) >> 32) + M on ARM BE, whose adc r0,r0,#M is the code for x + (M << 32 | K). An int that shifts, masks, offsets, negates or multiplies that high word, applies a literal operation to a value the low word never reads, or reads the low half of the product whose high half is in the second register keeps its int (w18 hash64, w21 sum3_shr33, w22, w23, w24)
tradeoff.read_as_int_wrong_for_long_long: (u64)x << 32 (a dead zero in the second register), ((u64)(x^K)<<32)|K, a long long whose low word also feeds a call, (u64)a + b with only the carry in the high word, a long long whose high word is a literal 0 or 1 a branch chose, a long long whose high word is a literal or a flag beside a low-word sum whose carry a branch tests (u32 s = a + b; return s < a ? 0 : s; returning u64), and -O0 (v << 32) | (v >> 32) of a 64-bit local (reloaded like a truncation; swap64 on PowerPC and ARM BE -O0), a long long whose low word is a right shift of a value whose dropped bits also build its high word, and a long long returned beside an indirect jump flow could not follow whose low word the jump's code can read; a long long whose high word is a literal operation on a value its low word does not read (*p | 0xffULL << 32), a reworked high word beside its sum's low word (((s >> 33) << 32) | (u32)s), and a 64-bit literal sum whose literal the compiler adds after the carry (MIPS gcc (u64)a + 0x7fffffffffffffff at -O1 to -Os); as on main in both modes
tradeoff.witness_count: w2-w10, big, ib, w13-w24 and dv (PowerPC, SPARC, ARM BE at its default architecture, ARMv6 and ARMv7, MIPS gcc and, for w13-w24, MIPS clang, -O0 to -Os; round trips compiled with gcc and clang; Thumb-2 BE builds measure nothing): 1,193 builds fixed, 79 turned wrong, all trade-off rows (sum_hi 18, sub_hi 9, mulhi_k 10, xk_hi_add 10 on ARM BE, umulh_sum 8, ud641 and ud6700417 7 each, hi64k 6, mulhi, mulhi_s, mul_hi_s, hi_of_mul 1 each); against the previous version 197 builds it turned wrong print as on main and 54 of its fixes are given up (ld_or 28, xy_hi_sh 23, xk_max 3); the comparison and truncation rules give up swap64 (PowerPC/ARM BE -O0) and the range-check rule zsum_chk/zs_chk2 (ARM BE -O1 to -Os)
tradeoff.why_default_on: in 24,257 real functions of nine corpora (e2fsprogs, coreutils and gnulib, libexpat, libbsd, dpkg, diffutils, findutils, sysvinit, Lua, libselinux, iproute2, rsyslog, openssh, bash, cronie, libedit, grep, kmod, shadow, zlib, dash, gnutls, base-passwd, gzip; DWARF-checked) no function whose DWARF return type is int or a pointer changes value, while their 64-bit returns are fixed.
